newsitem.title: UK: Copper price set for explosive rebound -- Bain.
newsitem.headline: Copper price set for explosive rebound -- Bain.

text.p: Copper prices are currently trading some 20/30 cents per lb below fundamentally justified levels leaving the market potentially set for an explosive rebound, brokers Bain and Co said.

In a special report on the copper market Bain analysts Wiktor Bielski and Alan Williamson said that prices are under levels that should prevail, based on a 15-year relationship between total reported stocks and prices.
"With the effects of the Sumitomo Corp scandal now fading, this discount is excessive and no longer justified," it said.
London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks have fallen to the lowest levels for some six years, and total stocks are now at 3.4 weeks consumption -- below critical levels, Bain said.
Prices have failed to react higher as major short sellers have exploited technicals factors in the post-Sumitomo market.

"However, falling stocks and rising demand could result in a severe physical squeeze in the next three to six months, which would overwhelm the price cap and drive prices above $1.00 per lb," Bain said.
Bain is forecasting a deficit of 100,000/200,000 tonnes in 1996, contrary to most other forecasts of a 200,000/300,000 tonne surplus and despite higher exports from the CIS.

"We disagree with ongoing forecasts of large surpluses in 1997 and 1998, which we believe understate Chinese imports and overstate production growth. We expect market deficits in both years," Bain said.
Looking at stocks, Bain expect these to fall to all-time lows of just three weeks consumption in 1998, supporting sharply higher prices.
As fundamentals regain control the "Sumitomo-discount' should be closed and the longer the short sellers postpone this the more intense the price rally will be, Bain said.
"We therefore expect copper prices to surprise on the upside, with an average of $102.50 a lb in 1997, rising to $107.50 a lb in 1998," Bain said.
